# compact objects upward in order along gravity; represent 10x10 board
R=C=10
objs=[(3,[(1,2),(1,3)]),(6,[(1,7),(2,7)]),(7,[(2,5),(3,5)]),(8,[(3,1),(3,2)]),(6,[(4,8),(4,9)]),(3,[(5,4),(5,5)]),(9,[(6,2),(7,2)]),(4,[(6,8),(7,8)]),(3,[(8,0),(9,0)]),(1,[(8,5),(8,6)]),(5,[(9,7),(9,8)])]
# order objects by nearest leading edge (topmost); repeatedly process in order, drop upward to min legal row, preserving shape.
board=[[-1]*C for _ in range(R)]
for i,(v,cells) in enumerate(objs):
 for r,c in cells: board[r][c]=i
# gravity settle objects from top to bottom, ordering by min row, tie by min col
for i,(v,cells) in sorted(enumerate(objs),key=lambda x:(min(r for r,c in x[1][1]),min(c for r,c in x[1][1]))):
 # erase current cells
 for r,c in cells: board[r][c]=-1
 dr=min(r for r,c in cells)
 # attempt move upward until blocked/wall
 shift=0
 while True:
  nr=min(r for r,c in cells)+shift-1
  if nr<0: break
  candidate=[(r+shift-1,c) for r,c in cells]
  if any(board[r][c]!=-1 for r,c in candidate): break
  shift-=1
 for r,c in cells: board[r+shift][c]=i
print('\n'.join(' '.join('.' if x<0 else str(objs[x][0]) for x in row) for row in board))

]

        if min(r for r,c in nxt)<0 or any(grid[r][c] for r,c in nxt): break
        cells=nxt
    for r,c in cells:
